hot.title: Self-Distilled Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: Researchers at Zhejiang University, Meituan, and Tsinghua University developed Self-Distilled Agentic Reinforcement Learning (SDAR), a method that robustly integrates on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) with reinforcement learning for multi-turn Large Language Model agents. This approach utilizes a token-level gating mechanism to selectively apply teacher guidance, achieving up to a 9.4% improvement in success rates on ALFWorld and outperforming other hybrid methods while effectively internalizing skills without needing them at inference.

hot.title: FutureSim: Replaying World Events to Evaluate Adaptive Agents
hot.summary: Researchers developed FutureSim, an environment that replays real-world events from timestamped news to evaluate AI agents' long-horizon adaptive forecasting capabilities. The benchmark revealed significant room for improving test-time adaptation in frontier models, with GPT 5.5 achieving 25% top-1 accuracy but many open-weight models demonstrating negative Brier skill scores.

hot.title: SANA-WM: Efficient Minute-Scale World Modeling with Hybrid Linear Diffusion Transformer
hot.summary: NVIDIA researchers developed SANA-WM, a 2.6B-parameter open-source world model capable of generating high-fidelity, one-minute 720p videos with precise 6-DoF camera control. The system achieves visual quality comparable to larger industrial baselines while significantly reducing data, training, and inference costs, demonstrating strong performance on a new 60-second world-model benchmark.

hot.title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
hot.summary: Researchers at PricewaterhouseCoopers empirically investigated the effectiveness of retrieval strategies for LLM agents, focusing on how lexical (grep) and semantic (vector) search interact with different agent architectures and tool output delivery methods. The study reveals that grep often achieves higher accuracy when tool results are delivered inline, and that overall agent performance is heavily influenced by the agent's specific orchestration layer.

hot.title: ATLAS: Agentic or Latent Visual Reasoning? One Word is Enough for Both
hot.summary: ATLAS is a visual reasoning framework that integrates discrete 'functional tokens' into autoregressive Vision-Language Models, enabling them to represent and execute visual operations within a standard generation loop. This method allows models to perform complex interleaved visual reasoning more efficiently and interpretably than prior approaches, leading to improved performance on benchmarks like WeMath and BLINK.

hot.title: Causal Forcing++: Scalable Few-Step Autoregressive Diffusion Distillation for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
hot.summary: Causal Forcing++ introduces a scalable method for real-time interactive video generation, enabling frame-wise autoregression with just one to two sampling steps. This framework achieves superior video quality and dynamics while reducing first-frame latency by 50% and increasing throughput by approximately 1.4 times compared to prior methods.

hot.title: Articraft: An Agentic System for Scalable Articulated 3D Asset Generation
hot.summary: Articraft, an agentic system developed by researchers at the University of Cambridge and University of Oxford, generates simulation-ready articulated 3D assets by having a large language model write Python programs. This system produced Articraft-10K, a dataset of over 10,000 curated articulated 3D models spanning 245 categories, shown to improve 3D articulation estimation and enable robust robotic simulations.

hot.title: δδδ-mem: Efficient Online Memory for Large Language Models
hot.summary: δ-mem introduces an efficient online memory mechanism for large language models, augmenting frozen backbones by compressing historical information into a fixed-size associative state that dynamically steers attention via low-rank corrections. The system achieved the highest overall performance among compared memory mechanisms, boosting the Qwen3-4B-Instruct backbone's average score by 4.87 percentage points to 51.66% on memory-intensive benchmarks while incurring minimal parameter overhead.

hot.title: Beyond Individual Intelligence: Surveying Collaboration, Failure Attribution, and Self-Evolution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
hot.summary: Researchers from multiple institutions including Xi'an Jiaotong University and The University of Sydney provide a comprehensive survey of large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) using a "LIFE progression" framework. This framework integrates individual agent capabilities, multi-agent collaboration, failure attribution, and self-evolution, highlighting their causal interdependencies and advocating for a closed-loop system for continuous improvement.

hot.title: Warp-as-History: Generalizable Camera-Controlled Video Generation from One Training Video
hot.summary: The framework Warp-as-History facilitates camera-controlled video generation by repurposing a pretrained model's visual-history conditioning pathway with camera-induced geometric warps. This approach achieves competitive camera adherence and superior visual quality after fine-tuning with only a single video, reducing reliance on extensive datasets and complex inference procedures.

hot.title: World Action Models: The Next Frontier in Embodied AI
hot.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) represent an emerging paradigm in embodied AI, unifying predictive physical understanding with action generation to enable agents to anticipate environment changes under their interventions. This comprehensive survey provides a formal definition, a structured architectural taxonomy, and a systematic analysis of data ecosystems and evaluation protocols for WAMs, outlining critical challenges and future research directions.

hot.title: ELF: Embedded Language Flows
hot.summary: Embedded Language Flows (ELF) establishes a continuous diffusion language model paradigm utilizing Flow Matching, achieving competitive generative quality in tasks like machine translation and summarization while requiring approximately 10 times fewer training tokens and fewer inference steps than existing baselines.

hot.title: DiLA: Disentangled Latent Action World Models
Qwen-Image-VAE-2.0 Technical Report
hot.summary: The Qwen Team developed Qwen-Image-VAE-2.0, a suite of high-compression Variational Autoencoders achieving state-of-the-art image reconstruction quality at f16 and f32 spatial compression ratios. The models demonstrate superior text fidelity on a new benchmark, with Qwen-Image-VAE-2.0-f16c128 surpassing leading f8 VAEs in Normalized Edit Distance (0.9617 vs 0.9546), while ensuring a generation-friendly latent space for downstream diffusion models.

hot.title: Achieving Gold-Medal-Level Olympiad Reasoning via Simple and Unified Scaling
hot.summary: The SU-01 model, a 30B-A3B architecture from Shanghai AI Laboratory and collaborators, demonstrates gold-medal-level reasoning performance in International Physics and Mathematics Olympiads by applying a three-stage training and inference pipeline. This system achieved scores exceeding gold medal thresholds for IPhO 2024/2025 and IMO/USAMO 2025/2026, often matching or surpassing top human competitors.

hot.title: Harnessing Agentic Evolution
hot.summary: Researchers from The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) and DeepWisdom, among others, developed AEVO, a harnessed meta-editing framework for agentic evolution. It reformulates evolution as an interactive environment where an external meta-agent revises the underlying evolution mechanism, achieving superior performance on open-ended optimization tasks and standard benchmarks.

hot.title: OpenDeepThink: Parallel Reasoning via Bradley--Terry Aggregation
hot.summary: OpenDeepThink introduces a population-based framework for Large Language Models that enhances reasoning capabilities by combining parallel candidate generation with Bradley–Terry aggregated pairwise LLM judgments and feedback-driven mutation. This verifier-free approach led to a 405-point Elo gain on Codeforces competitive programming benchmarks for Gemini 3.1 Pro and improved accuracy on objective reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Process Reward Models That Think
likes.summary: This research introduces THINKPRM, a generative process reward model that enables large language models to provide verbalized, long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification for their reasoning steps. The model, developed by a collaboration including University of Michigan and LG AI Research, achieves high performance with orders of magnitude less step-level supervision than traditional discriminative models, while significantly improving reliability and generalizability.

likes.title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report
likes.summary: Microsoft Research introduces BitNet b1.58 2B4T, the first open-source, natively trained 1-bit Large Language Model at the 2-billion parameter scale, pre-trained on 4 trillion tokens. This model achieves competitive performance with full-precision LLMs of similar size while requiring substantially less memory (0.4 GB), exhibiting lower decoding latency (29 ms), and consuming significantly less energy.

likes.title: A Survey on Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models: What, How,  Where, and How Well?
likes.summary: A comprehensive survey introduces a unified, four-axis taxonomy to systematically organize the rapidly growing field of Test-Time Scaling (TTS) in Large Language Models (LLMs). This work provides a structured framework for classifying methods, offers practical guidelines for deployment, and identifies critical open challenges for future research in enhancing LLM performance during inference.

likes.title: Scaling Laws for Native Multimodal Models
likes.summary: Researchers at Apple conducted a comprehensive study on scaling laws for native multimodal models, demonstrating that early-fusion architectures trained from scratch can achieve comparable performance to late-fusion approaches while offering superior training efficiency and lower deployment costs. Integrating Mixture of Experts into these early-fusion designs further enhances performance and enables implicit specialization to different modalities.

likes.title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
likes.summary: This paper introduces 'sleep-time compute,' a method for optimizing Large Language Model inference by pre-computing insights about persistent contexts during idle periods. The approach reduces test-time compute by approximately 5 times for similar accuracy on reasoning tasks and decreases average query cost by up to 2.5 times when amortized across multiple queries over the same context.

likes.title: Why do LLMs attend to the first token?
likes.summary: Large Language Models learn attention sinks, often directed at the first token, as a fundamental mechanism to prevent information degradation, known as over-mixing and representational collapse, which is crucial for maintaining performance, particularly in processing long contexts. Removing these sinks at inference time severely impacts model utility across various tasks.

likes.title: Vision as LoRA
likes.summary: Vision as LoRA (VoRA), developed by ByteDance, proposes an encoder-free architecture for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by internalizing vision capabilities directly into LLMs using mergeable LoRA layers. This approach achieves performance comparable to encoder-based models with near-zero additional inference cost and supports arbitrary image resolutions, all while demonstrating stable and data-efficient training through block-wise distillation and bi-directional attention for vision.

likes.title: Frame Context Packing and Drift Prevention in Next-Frame-Prediction Video Diffusion Models
likes.summary: FramePack introduces a framework for next-frame-prediction video diffusion models, employing progressive context packing to manage memory and novel anti-drifting sampling strategies. This system enables the generation of thousands of coherent video frames while maintaining visual quality and mitigating the accumulation of errors.

likes.title: Real AI Agents with Fake Memories: Fatal Context Manipulation Attacks on Web3 Agents
likes.summary: A study by Princeton University and the Sentient Foundation formalized "memory injection" as a stealthy context manipulation attack against LLM-powered Web3 agents. The research empirically demonstrated that these attacks achieve higher success rates than prompt injection and bypass current prompt-level defenses, with fine-tuning showing improved robustness, particularly on the CrAIBench benchmark and ElizaOS.

likes.title: Holistic Fusion: Task- and Setup-Agnostic Robot Localization and State  Estimation with Factor Graphs
likes.summary: A factor graph-based framework enables task-agnostic robot state estimation by jointly optimizing local and global states while automatically aligning multiple reference frames, demonstrating real-time performance across diverse platforms (ANYmal, RACER, HEAP) and environments while handling sensor drift through random walk modeling.

likes.title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
likes.summary: NVIDIA researchers developed GR00T N1, an open foundation Vision-Language-Action model for generalist humanoid robots. The model achieves robust performance on real GR-1 humanoid robots and simulation tasks, utilizing a 'data pyramid' strategy for efficient training and strong generalization across diverse robot embodiments and scenarios.

likes.title: Kimi-VL Technical Report
likes.summary: Kimi-VL is an efficient open-source Mixture-of-Experts vision-language model that achieves competitive performance across diverse multimodal tasks, often matching or exceeding larger proprietary and open-source models with only 2.8 billion activated parameters. Its "Thinking" variants enhance reasoning, while the architecture supports 128K extended context and native-resolution visual inputs.

likes.title: I-Con: A Unifying Framework for Representation Learning
likes.summary: Researchers at MIT, Google, and Microsoft developed I-Con, an information-theoretic framework that unifies over 23 diverse machine learning loss functions, including those for dimensionality reduction, contrastive learning, and supervised learning, under a single KL-divergence objective. This unified perspective enabled the creation of new debiasing strategies and a novel unsupervised clustering method, "Debiased InfoNCE Clustering," which achieved state-of-the-art performance on ImageNet-1K with gains of up to 7.8% in Hungarian accuracy.

likes.title: It's All Connected: A Journey Through Test-Time Memorization,  Attentional Bias, Retention, and Online Optimization
likes.summary: A unified framework from Google Research introduces "Miras" for sequence modeling that reinterprets attention mechanisms and forgetting gates as forms of memory optimization, leading to three new architectures (Moneta, Yaad, and Memora) that demonstrate improved performance on language modeling and recall-intensive tasks while providing theoretical insights into existing models.

likes.title: SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models
likes.summary: Hugging Face and Stanford researchers develop SmolVLM, a family of compact multimodal models that process both images and videos while requiring less than 1GB of GPU memory for the smallest 256M parameter variant, achieving competitive performance through optimized architecture design and training strategies that specifically target resource-constrained environments.

likes.title: SPRING: Systematic Profiling of Randomly Interconnected Neural Networks  Generated by HLS
likes.summary: Northwestern University researchers develop SPRING, a profiling framework for FPGA-based streaming machine learning accelerators that enables concurrent monitoring of over 200 internal signals while maintaining synchronization with data streams, integrated into the hls4ml open-source tool for automated analysis of randomly interconnected neural networks.

likes.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
likes.summary: This paper introduces MAST, an empirically derived taxonomy of 14 multi-agent system failure modes, and MAST-Data, a dataset of 1642 annotated execution traces. The work reveals that failures in multi-agent LLM systems primarily stem from system design issues and inter-agent misalignment, rather than solely from underlying large language model limitations.

likes.title: Describe Anything: Detailed Localized Image and Video Captioning
likes.summary: NVIDIA and UC Berkeley researchers introduce DAM (Describe Anything Model), a vision-language architecture that generates detailed captions for specific regions in images and videos through a focal prompt mechanism and localized vision backbone, achieving state-of-the-art performance across 7 benchmarks while addressing data scarcity through a semi-supervised learning pipeline.

likes.title: Multi-Token Attention
likes.summary: Researchers at FAIR, Meta, introduced Multi-Token Attention, an architectural modification that enables LLMs to condition attention weights on multiple query and key vectors simultaneously, improving long-context information retrieval and general language understanding with minimal parameter overhead.

likes.title: InternVL3: Exploring Advanced Training and Test-Time Recipes for  Open-Source Multimodal Models
likes.summary: InternVL3 establishes a new native multimodal pre-training paradigm for MLLMs, allowing the model to jointly acquire visual and linguistic capabilities from the outset. This approach achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models, reaching 72.2 on the MMMU benchmark, and demonstrates strong competitiveness with leading proprietary models across a wide range of multimodal tasks.
